gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 100 Ws Godox V100 gives about 0.4 stop more light per pop than the 76 Ws V1Pro, yet both flashes deliver about the same total light per charge (V100 40,000 J vs V1Pro 38,000 J, from the same 7.2 V/2980 mAh ≈ 21.5 Wh battery). That works out to $0.66 per full-power flash for the V1Pro and $0.87 for the V100.
standout_why: I checked the cited and top results. cameraegg.org 'Best Diffuser for Godox V1 Flash' (2026-10-09) prices the AK-R11 ($7.90), AK-R22 ($26.90), ML-CD15 ($29) and AK-R1 ($49) domes. It says outright that it gives no flash guide number, full-power flashes per charge or recycle time, and no light loss in stops. The cited B&H AK-R11 specs page returned HTTP 403, so I couldn't read it. ChatGPT's own answer names the Godox V1 with no numbers at all. None of these pages compares output, flashes per charge or cost per flash across the round-head flashes that fit these domes.
decides: A dome diffuser costs light, so a flash with more power per pop helps. The V100 gives about 0.4 stop more per pop (log2(100/76) = 0.40) for $20 more, but it delivers 100 fewer full-power flashes per charge (400 vs 500), recycles slower (1.7 s vs 1.3 s) and weighs 616 g with its battery. For event shooting with a dome, the V1Pro stays the pick: more pops, faster recycle, lower cost per flash. The V100 is the pick only if the shopper bounces off high ceilings or uses the larger AK-R22 dome and needs the extra 0.4 stop.
